To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the N-terminal domain of schwannomin folds into a structure, that this structure is disrupted by several NF2 mutations, that disruption of this structure results in loss of membrane localization and actins association of the protein and that these two cellular functions are directly linked to each other.
a structured domain entirely within the N-terminal part of schwannomin is necessary and sufficient for the protein to localize beneath the plasma membrane and to bind to actin.
the N-terminal domain of schwannomin folds into a compact structure that is necessary and sufficient for membrane localization and action binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel schwannomin domain, the N-terminal domain fold, that is essential for the protein to perform its normal function in cells.
a previously unrecognized domain in schwannomins that is essential for the protein's membrane localization and acto-myosin binding.
the characterization of the first structured domain of schwannomin, and its role in schwannomin function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal domain is the first structural domain of schwannomin and its folding is critical for schwannomin function.
the N-terminus of schwannomin has a role in membrane localization and act in binding.
the N-terminal half, including the FERM domain, is essential for schwannomin function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminal domain of schwannomin is a highly structured region that is critical for the protein to function normally.
the N-terminal domain of schwannomin folds into a structured domain, which is required for normal cellular localization and actin binding.
the N-terminal domain of schwannomin is an autonomous folded domain whose structure is essential for the proper localization and function of schwannomin at the membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal domain of the NF2 protein is a highly structured region that plays a critical role in schwannomin's cellular functions.
the FERM domain of schwannomin is not sufficient to confer the full spectrum of cellular activities of the protein.
schwannomin, like the related ERM and EBP50 proteins, is a highly dynamic molecule, with a folded N-terminal domain that is essential for normal membrane localization and actins association.
